findings: At four features per group, increasing groups from 4 to 8 to 16 reduced mean logit MAE from 0.11062 to 0.08800 to 0.06984 while Q.ANT accuracy increased from 0.8207 to 0.83643 to 0.84670.
Increasing to 28 groups did not continue the numerical-error improvement: mean logit MAE rose to 0.07614 despite lower first-stage fan-in.
The 16x2 model used only 15146 parameters and reached 0.83123 mean Q.ANT accuracy.
The 16x8 model achieved the highest mean Q.ANT accuracy, 0.85393, but had higher logit MAE than 16x4.
Five of six candidates were non-dominated under the experiment's accuracy-versus-parameter Pareto objective.
interpretation: The search supports a useful low-fan-in region but falsifies a simple monotonic rule that smaller first-stage fan-in always improves numerical agreement. Because increasing group count reduces stage-1 accumulation while increasing the dimensionality accumulated by the stage-2 head, the full hierarchy is a plausible explanatory variable.
next_research_direction: Measure numerical discrepancy separately after stage 1 and after stage 2 across controlled group counts, and compare observed errors with each stage's accumulated term count.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
The search jointly changes first-stage fan-in and second-stage input width when group count changes.
Three seeds and FashionMNIST do not establish generality.
